clients.name: WhispererKit, the shared Swift networking package
clients.deployment: Linked into the macOS app (working), the Linux app (frozen) and the iOS app (not shipped); its calls reach users through the macOS build.
clients.notes: Base URL `https://whisperer.one/v1` from `Info.plist`; paths are appended without a trailing slash. TLS public keys are pinned (`Config.swift:174-177`): the production certificate must keep one of the two pinned SPKI hashes (Let's Encrypt YE1 or ISRG Root YE). The Linux transport follows no redirects, keeps no cookies and sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, so a redirect or a compressed body on any API endpoint breaks it. Dates must be ISO-8601 with a time zone; meeting note and import responses use camelCase keys (`draftMarkdown`, `jobId`, `fileName`, `meetingId`). UUIDs in paths and in `sid`/`hub_id` are upper case. `POST me/storage/knowledge`, `PUT me/models/roles/{role}` and `POST knowledge/sources/{id}/sync` must answer with a JSON body, not 204. On `/v1/ws/realtime` a 401 or 403 handshake stops reconnecting. `/v1/ws/user` `hello` always sends `client: "desktop_macos"`. `GET /v1/scripts` must keep answering 404 (feature hidden). Calls made from the kit modules Hub, Knowledge, Leo, Proactive, Rooms, Search and Workspace are recorded but do not make an endpoint must-keep: the macOS app references no type declared in those modules, so only the unshipped iOS app reaches them.
